memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: He answered, "I heard you in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid." — Gen 3:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is Adam's answer to God's gentle "Where are you?" And in this short reply we hear the sound of the human heart after sin: "I heard... I was afraid... I hid."

Notice what fear has done. Before, Adam walked with God without a trace of terror. Now the nearness of God fills him with dread, and his first instinct is to run and cover himself. Sin has turned fellowship into fear. Adam blames his fear on his nakedness — "because I was naked" — but the real problem was deeper than that. His body had not changed; his heart had. It was guilt, not nakedness, that truly made him hide.

We do the same. When we have done wrong, we often become experts at managing the surface — explaining, excusing, hiding the outward thing — while the deeper guilt goes untouched. But God is never fooled by our fig leaves. He sees the heart beneath.

Dear friend, here is the tender mercy of the Gospel. The fear that drove Adam into the trees is exactly the fear Jesus came to remove. "Perfect love drives out fear" (1 Jn 4:18). Because Christ has borne our guilt at the cross, we no longer need to hide when God draws near. We can come to Him honestly, not with fear, but with confidence — welcomed, forgiven, and loved.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When you feel God drawing near after you've sinned, is your instinct fear or trust?
2. Are there surface things you manage to avoid facing the deeper guilt underneath?
3. How does the love of Christ free you from hiding in fear?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I confess that fear and guilt often make me want to hide from You. Thank You that through Jesus my guilt is taken away, so I can come to You without fear. Replace my hiding with honest trust, and my fear with the confidence of Your love. Amen.
